_comment: ILLUSTRATIVE, EXPLICITLY NON-PRODUCTION cloud-transport configuration — NOT ACTIVATED,
NOT DEPLOYED, and no path below is claimed to exist on any host. Nothing in this
repository reads this file automatically. The one executable that can read a file of this
shape (E3J6C: node ops/backup/eanhl-backup-cloud.mjs --config <path> --artifact-base <base>)
has no shebang, no executable bit, and no package script, and nothing schedules, deploys or
invokes it. It and the libraries beneath it (E3J4-E3J6C) have only been exercised against
local fakes and disposable local probes, and are not activated —
see docs/planning/proton-drive-cloud-transport-architecture.md §12.
There are no defaults: every key below is required, and a missing key is a hard error.
Every path, size, timeout, retry count, containment selector and remote-root value in
this file is a made-up, non-production placeholder for shape-validation only.
U12 (the three readback byte ceilings and which containment mechanism is proven on the
real host), U13 (timeouts, cancellation grace, retry counts and backoff) and U14
(the real remote.root/account namespace) are all still UNRESOLVED — see
docs/planning/proton-drive-transport-feasibility.md §9. Nothing here resolves them.
readback.containment is a DECLARATION only: writing 'rlimit_fsize' here does not itself
prove the kernel enforces that limit against the real CLI binary on any host — that proof
is a deployment prerequisite this file cannot satisfy (memo §3.3).
This file contains no account identifier, e-mail address, token, passphrase, session
path, or recovery material. credentials.backend names a backend selector only; the
uploader consumes an already-unlocked credential context and never reads a secret from
any file this configuration names.
executable and expectedSha512 are illustrative placeholders. expectedSha512 is NOT the
hash of any real, installed, or reviewed binary — see the E3J1 memo §6.3 for why this
pin is required rather than optional, and §6.1-6.2 for why '--version' is not used as
the primary identity check.
'backend' is a SELECTOR only, never a secret. Credential unlocking and storage
mechanics are entirely outside the uploader's scope (memo §7.2); that mechanism is its
own separate, not-yet-authorized session (E3J9).
An illustrative, non-production placeholder path. The real remote.root/account
namespace is UNRESOLVED (U14) and is an operator decision, not a code decision.
Read-only to the uploader; this would be the producer's own destination.dir. This
path is illustrative only and is not claimed to exist.
Where attempt-scoped cloud-attestation files would be written, one per attempt,
O_CREAT|O_EXCL, never rewritten (memo §4.2, §9). Illustrative path only.
Three SEPARATE, illustrative, non-production ceilings (U12) — never derived from one
another, each INCLUSIVE (a role of exactly its ceiling is acceptable). containment is a
declaration only (see the top-level _comment); neither value below has been proven to
enforce anything on any real host.
rlimitWrapper (E3J6A) is required for 'rlimit_fsize' and must be null for 'quota_mount'.
It names the RLIMIT_FSIZE wrapper (prlimit) that runs in front of the CLI with the exact
per-role ceiling as both soft and hard limit, pinned by SHA-512 like the CLI. The path
and pin below are illustrative placeholders, NOT the hash of any real binary. A runtime
canary refuses to proceed unless this wrapper demonstrably enforces the smallest ceiling
on this host; 'quota_mount' is accepted as shape only and refused at runtime.
Illustrative, non-production timings (U13). cancelGraceMs must be smaller than
operationTimeoutMs; the values below satisfy that shape rule and nothing more.
lockFile (E3J6C) is the run lock: created O_EXCL mode 0600 inside an operator-provisioned,
trusted (0700, owner-only) directory that the uploader never creates; held from before
containment through every attempt and backoff. It is never reclaimed automatically — a
lock left behind needs operator reconciliation (memo §4.7).
Illustrative, non-production retry policy (U13) — an operator reliability and
debris-accumulation decision, not something this example resolves.
Consumed by E3J6C: automatic retry happens ONLY after a definite zero-transfer name
collision (R1), each retry with a fresh attempt id and remote namespace, bounded by both
ceilings, with this fixed backoff between attempts and none after the last.
Illustrative, non-production capacity floor. backingVolume is required-but-nullable,
the same WSL-aware rule the producer and acceptor configs already use — see
ops/backup/eanhl-backup.example.json for why 'df' can lie on a sparse-VHDX mount.
